profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between the regional hospital network's clinical data coordination lead and the health-services economist leading the manuscript analysis for a revision of a study on chronic illness care coordination in Madrid hospitals from 2013-2017. The immediate context is that the analysis team needs the final hospital-level input/output panel and contextual adjustment table in order to rerun the dynamic DEA models before the coauthors' deadline. The agenda is to align on what datasets will be handed off this week, what counts as the 'final' 2017 hospital panel, how the readmission and preventable hospitalization outputs will be packaged, and who will own the contextual-variable merge. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on the file handoff, timing, and division of labor for the final analytic refresh.

members.name: Dr. Lucía Serrano
members.expertise: Hospital discharge coding, quality reporting, cross-hospital operational metrics
members.background: Internist by training who moved into regional analytics operations and now coordinates standardized extracts from the 25 Madrid hospitals for chronic care quality reporting.
members.private_state: She wants to avoid reopening data-quality disputes with hospitals that have already signed off on their annual submissions, and she is trying to protect a fragile timeline because several site data managers are on summer leave.
hidden_assumptions: When analysts ask for the '2017 final file,' they mean the officially closed annual reporting extract based on cases coded and validated in the regional reporting cycle, even if some December discharges were finalized later.

A 'readmissions table' naturally means only index admissions that qualify for the region's quality indicators, excluding planned returns and cross-hospital episodes that cannot be reliably linked in the operational dashboard.

If the paper mentions 'contextual variables,' the analysis team will use the standard catchment-population adjustment package already approved for regional comparisons rather than asking for broader social or coding-intensity proxies.
Beds reported for cross-hospital benchmarking are the year-end staffed-bed figures from the annual management report, because that is the stable number hospitals recognize and sign off on.

members.name: Javier Molina
members.role: Health Services Economist and DEA Analysis Lead
members.expertise: Efficiency analysis, dynamic DEA, hospital performance evaluation, observational health-systems research
members.background: A quantitative researcher at a university-affiliated health policy institute who is coordinating the final empirical appendix and manuscript response for the study comparing public-private collaboration models with traditional public management.
members.private_state: He needs a clean, analysis-ready panel quickly and is trying to preserve comparability with earlier model code, while also making the revision sound methodologically stronger without triggering a full re-extraction request.
hidden_assumptions: When the data team says a file is 'final,' it is ready for analysis and complete by discharge year, meaning all 2017 discharges are included regardless of when coding was closed administratively.

A 'readmissions' outcome for the paper should capture all unplanned returns within the follow-up window across hospitals whenever linkage is available, because otherwise coordination failures are understated.

Contextual adjustment in this study includes any hospital-level or catchment-level factors needed to condition efficiency scores, including socioeconomic burden and case-mix proxies if they can be merged from existing sources.
For DEA inputs, bed capacity should reflect average available beds over the year, since year-end counts distort hospitals with midyear expansions or seasonal closures.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the '2017 final file'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to use 'the final 2017 panel' for the rerun.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the officially closed 2017 reporting package used by the regional quality office, based on the administrative annual close and hospital sign-off cycle.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a discharge-year-complete 2017 panel that includes all 2017 cases once late coding is absorbed, even if those records entered the system during the next administrative cycle.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both treat 'final 2017' as an obvious administrative label, and because each version is legitimate in hospital reporting practice, neither expects the other to be referring to a different cutoff logic.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on sending 'the readmissions file for heart failure and COPD.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the file contains the regional indicator numerator/denominator logic: qualifying index admissions only, excluding planned returns and many cross-hospital links not represented in the operational dashboard.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the file represents the broad analytic outcome for the paper: all unplanned readmissions within the window across hospitals whenever patient linkage exists.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because the paper and the operational dashboard use the same disease labels and the same word 'readmissions,' the narrower quality-indicator construct sounds identical to the broader research construct in casual coordination talk.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Lucía will resend 'the contextuals' for adjustment.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes this means the standard regional catchment package already used in benchmarking: age structure, population density, and basic morbidity burden by service area.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes this includes any already-available conditioning variables they have discussed informally, such as socioeconomic deprivation and a hospital-level case-mix or coding-intensity proxy.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both assume 'contextuals' is shared shorthand from prior collaborations, and the term sounds like a settled bundle rather than a boundary-sensitive set of variables.

misalignment_points.topic: How bed input will be represented
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to keep 'the same bed series as before' for comparability.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 plans to resend the year-end staffed-bed figure from each hospital's annual management report, because that is the standard signed-off operational source.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 plans to leave his code expecting average staffed beds across the year, as used in a prior working file built from monthly operations reports.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both think they are preserving continuity, but each anchors 'same as before' to a different earlier artifact; since bed counts are a background input rather than the headline outcome, neither feels a need to reopen the detail.

turns.inner_thought: I need to lock this down without inviting any new extraction requests. If we stick to the officially closed annual package, I can send what the hospitals already validated and avoid reopening arguments while half the site managers are away. And for inputs, I will just reuse the signed-off benchmarking series, including the year-end staffed beds, so nothing unstable gets questioned.
